Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Nitin Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Nand Kishor Mishra, learned counsel for the informant and Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.258 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act at Police Station- Rath, District Hamirpur with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, on 07.03.2020, the son of the applicant Abhilash Arya is stated to have married the deceased person as per Hindu Rites and the applicant alongwith other family members are stated to have subjected her to cruelty for demand of dowry of Rs.10 lakhs, thereby leading to her death on 01.06.2023.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

He has strong alibi as he was working in the office of Block Development Officer, Rath,
District Hamirpur.
Learned counsel has further stated that the case of the applicant is at a different footing to the husband Abhilash Arya.
The cause of death has been found to be asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging, as such no role can be assigned to the applicant of causing her death.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

7. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
8. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

entities.text: Kanhaiya Lal Ayra vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv). that in case charge-sheet is submitted the applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial;
(v). that the applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness;
(vi). that the applicant shall appear before the trial court on each date fixed unless personal presence is exempted;
(vii). that in case of breach of any of the above conditions the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail.
9. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
Order Date :- 17.8.2023
Ravi Kant (Krishan Pahal, J.)
